reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational structure of behavior is built upon a hierarchy of goal objects, where each subordinate goal serves as a means toward a higher-order end. This hierarchical concatenation implies that behavior unfolds as a sequence of interlinked actions, each governed by an immanent determinant—either purposed or cognitive—that is not directly observable but inferred from behavioral variability. These determinants are functionally defined and can be subdivided into purposes and cognitions, which further split into readinesses and expectations. Inference emerges as a core modality through which these latent structures are accessed, operating alongside perception and mnemonization. The process of inference allows for the updating of expectations based on new experiences, enabling adaptive behavior. The failure mode arises when this hierarchical structure becomes misaligned due to environmental disruption or when inference fails to integrate past and present data effectively, leading to maladaptive responses.
